newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France ups exParis-HK-Taipei cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Air France ups exParis-HK-Taipei cargo rates.

text.p: Air France said it will increase ex-Paris cargo rates to Hong Kong and Tokyo by 50 centimes a kg, effective May 15.
The increases will work out at almost six percent for Hong Kong and just over three percent to Tokyo, an Air France Cargo official told Reuters.
"While the increases reflect buoyant demand, particularly to Hong Kong, they are partly a consequence of us withdrawing our fuel surcharge on cargo, effective April 15," the official said.
Neither Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd nor Japan Airlines Ltd, the major maindeck carriers from Paris to Hong Kong and Tokyo, along with Air France, had applied the fuel surcharge, the official added.

"Withdrawing the surcharge changed the "parity" between our rates and those of some other airlines. For example, on the Tokyo route, our rates are currently a little below those of JAL so the increase will more or less bring them into line with theirs."
JAL, with whom Air France operates joint freighter services between Paris and Tokyo, last increased its ex-Paris rates by three to four percent in January 1997.
On the Hong Kong route, Air France and Cathay, both of whom operate independently -- with three Boeing 747-200 freighter flights weekly each -- increased rates in March.
This was the Hong Kong airline's second rise in ex-Paris rates during the winter season having upped them to selected destinations in December 1996.
Air France had also increased ex-Paris rates to Taipei by 50 centimes a kg, the equivalent of around six percent, effective May 1, the official said.

"In the case of Taipei, the increases are more indicative of favourable market conditions - the fuel surcharge being much less a factor in that the other major carrier, Taiwanese, Eva Air, like ourselves, applied it and then withdrew it."
Air France operates a twice-weekly freighter service between Paris and Tapei.
Eva Air said its ex-Paris rates would remain unchanged despite Air France's raise and the buoyant level of demand on the route currently.
"It's unlikely we'll be upping rates before the atumn, as these having been a little above the market average since our last increase in October 1996," a Paris-based Eva cargo official told Reuters.
Eva Air operates a three times weekly Boeing 747 combi service between Paris and Taipei.-
